evidence.curator_note: Substrate as drawn: a 2-alkanone molecular ion printed as C3H7-CH(H)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-CH3 with the gamma hydrogen on C5 drawn EXPLICITLY and '+.' printed above the carbonyl oxygen. INSTANTIATION of the condensed 'C3H7' label (the page does not draw it out): it is taken as ISOPROPYL, making the compound 6-methyl-2-heptanone. That is not a guess -- the running text introducing this scheme rationalises 'the characteristic peaks in ... 6-methyl-2-heptanone (Figure 9.9)' and names 'a pair of acylium ions (m/z 113 and 43 in Figure 9.9) and a pair of alkyl ions (m/z 85 and 15)', which are exactly this equation's products. n-Propyl would give 2-octanone, an isomer with identical nominal masses at every step, so the drawing alone cannot distinguish them and the text is what settles it. LOCALIZATION (convention B): charge and odd electron are written on the oxygen where the page prints them, [C:2]=[O+:9]. Book draws 0 arc(s) on the molecular ion -- there is no fishhook anywhere on it; every arrow leaving it carries only a label. THIRD channel: the long horizontal arrow labelled with an italic 'i' running straight from the molecular ion to 'C6H13+ / m/z 85'. Charge-site-initiated cleavage of the SAME C2-C3 bond that the m/z 43 alpha channel breaks, but with the charge MIGRATING to the alkyl fragment: C6H13+ plus the neutral acetyl radical CH3-C(=O)., the complement of that channel's CH3CO+ / C6H13. pair. Note the page reaches m/z 85 by two different routes -- this one directly, and via CO loss from m/z 113 (IMS9-EQ9.26b) -- and draws both. Book draws 0 arc(s) and no product structure, so both moves are curator-supplied. ENCODING (why two one-electron moves rather than one 2-electron arrow): the precursor is an ODD-electron ion with charge AND radical on oxygen, while the products are an even-electron cation plus a neutral radical, so the oxygen must finish neutral and spin-paired. One electron of the breaking bond pairs with the oxygen's odd electron (move <1>) and the other stays on C2 as the acetyl radical's unpaired electron (move <2>); C3, having lost both, becomes the cation. The gate reports this as '(soft) ... consistent with a lone pair rather than radicals', which is the expected signature of that pairing, not a defect.
